reviewed_content.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

A morphism of algebraic spaces $Y\to X$ is *integral* if it is affine and integral after base change to every scheme over $X$. For a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space, an integral cover by a scheme is a surjective integral morphism $Y\to X$ with $Y$ a scheme. The *schematic locus* of an algebraic space is its largest open subspace representable by a scheme, when such a locus exists; a dense open scheme in $X$ means an open subscheme with dense image in $|X|$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A quasi-compact open immersion is an open embedding whose source is quasi-compact. A reduced closed subspace of an algebraic space is its uniquely determined reduced induced closed subspace. An étale stratification of $X$ by schemes is a finite chain of closed subspaces $\varnothing=Z_{-1}\subset Z_0\subset\cdots\subset Z_n=X$, whose locally closed differences $Z_r\setminus Z_{r-1}$ are schemes. An algebraic space is quasi-compact if it admits a finite affine étale cover, and quasi-separated when its diagonal is quasi-compact.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X \to Y$ be a surjective finite locally free
morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$. For $y \in |Y|$ the following are
equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $y$ is in the schematic locus of $Y$, and
\item there exists an affine open $U \subset X$
containing the preimage of $y$.
\end{enumerate}

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-etale-cover-dense-open-scheme}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
If there exists a finite, \'etale, surjective morphism
$U \to X$ where $U$ is a scheme, then there exists a dense open subspace
of $X$ which is a scheme.
